sources.title: Introducing Claude Sonnet 4.6
sources.evidence: February 17, 2026 launch announcement names Claude Sonnet 4.6, identifies it as a Sonnet model, and announces availability using claude-sonnet-4-6. Describes coding, computer use, agent planning and knowledge work, a 1M-token context window initially in beta, and both adaptive and extended thinking.

sources.title: Claude Sonnet 4.6 - Claude Platform Docs
sources.evidence: Exact-model page lists claude-sonnet-4-6, 1M-token context, adaptive thinking (with extended thinking marked deprecated), text and images to text, February 17, 2026 release, and Active (legacy) availability.

sources.title: Claude Sonnet 4.6 System Card
sources.evidence: Full 135-page card downloaded with curl and extracted with pdftotext. Introduction states evaluations use the final deployed Sonnet 4.6 unless specified otherwise; section 1.1 covers training and extended/adaptive thinking. Reviewed parameter and architecture mentions do not disclose production model size or neural architecture: effort parameters and multi-agent scaffolds are separate concepts.

sources.title: Claude Sonnet 5 System Card
sources.evidence: Full later card downloaded through official redirect to assets.claude.com/283ef97c476cf442c91d9a37d5b214242a55bb92.pdf after web-tool fetch failure and extracted with pdftotext. Contains numerous exact-name Sonnet 4.6 comparisons, including sections 6 and 8. No total/active parameter count or neural architecture for Sonnet 4.6 appears in the reviewed comparison and architecture/parameter material.

sources.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5 System Card
sources.evidence: Full later card downloaded with curl after web-tool content-length failure and extracted with pdftotext. No Sonnet 4.6-specific total/active parameter or architecture disclosure found; parameter references concern effort controls, not learned weight counts.

sources.title: Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models
sources.evidence: Methods and experiments name Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5, Opus 4.5 and Opus 4.6; no Sonnet 4.6 experiment is identified. This paper therefore does not establish Sonnet 4.6 architecture. Its layer indices are normalized percentages and its sparse interpretability features are not production parameter counts.

sources.title: GLM-5.3 and the spread of advanced cyber capabilities
sources.evidence: Explicitly states that Claude model weights are not publicly released or customizable and that weights are not provided to users. Used for general Claude weight-distribution policy, not for architecture or parameter estimates.

sources.title: Commercial Terms of Service
sources.evidence: Commercial terms govern Anthropic API services and reserve intellectual-property rights except those expressly granted. Supports proprietary service classification alongside explicit nonpublic-weight policy.

sources.title: PDF support
sources.evidence: Supported platforms and models section states that all active models support PDF processing. Explains PDF processing as extraction of text plus page images; exact Sonnet 4.6 model page separately confirms active availability.

sources.title: Tool use with Claude
sources.evidence: Official function-calling documentation explicitly lists Claude Sonnet 4.6 tool-choice modes auto/none and any/tool with their system-prompt token overhead.

name.note: Official display name matches the claude-sonnet-4-6 API identifier.

developer.note: First-party announcement and exact-model system card identify Anthropic as the developer.

family.note: Catalog normalization of the explicitly named Claude Sonnet model family; the launch describes Sonnet 4.6 as a Sonnet model and the Sonnet 5 card identifies it as the preceding Sonnet release.

release_date.note: Announcement gives February 17, 2026 and immediate availability; exact-model docs independently give the same release date.

open_weights.note: Explicit general Claude nonpublic-weight policy applies to this active Claude model. Hosted availability alone is not the basis for this classification.

license.note: Descriptive proprietary classification for this nonpublic-weight model offered under commercial service terms, not an asserted open-weight license.

parameters_b.note: No total production parameter count disclosed in the exact-model card, the later Sonnet 5 comparisons, or the later Sonnet 5.5 card. Targeted first-party exact-name parameter searches found no count; estimates are not substituted.

active_parameters_b.note: No active-per-token production parameter count disclosed in the reviewed original or later primary cards. Effort controls, generated-token limits and sparse interpretability features do not establish active model size.

architecture.note: No exact production Sonnet 4.6 neural architecture disclosed in reviewed cards or targeted first-party searches. Architecture mentions in the original card describe evaluation scaffolds or benchmark tasks. The workspace interpretability paper studies other named Claude versions, so transformer architecture is not transferred to this model.

context_window.note: Exact current model page gives 1M tokens; the launch announcement initially described this context window as beta.

modalities.note: Exact-model specs verify text/image input and text output. PDF is retained as the catalog-supported document input format, processed as text plus images; PDF docs cover active models and Sonnet 4.6 is explicitly active.

reasoning.note: Exact-model sources explicitly document adaptive and extended thinking; current specifications mark extended thinking deprecated. This is a dedicated reasoning capability rather than generic chain-of-thought prompting.

tool_call.note: Exact Sonnet 4.6 row documents supported tool-choice modes in official function-calling documentation.

description.value: Claude Sonnet model for coding, computer use and knowledge work, with adaptive reasoning and a 1M-token context window.
description.note: Neutral summary of documented use cases, adaptive thinking and context size; removes subjective workhorse and production-cost-control wording.

GLM-5.3 and the spread of advanced cyber capabilities

patch.notes: Total and active production parameter counts and exact Sonnet 4.6 architecture are undisclosed in reviewed primary sources. No architecture is inferred from another Claude model. PDF input denotes document processing through text and vision.

summary: Assessed all 14 fields against primary sources: 11 verified and 3 undisclosed. Confirms February 17, 2026 launch, 1M context, text/image/PDF input, text output, adaptive reasoning and tool calling. Adds proprietary classification and a neutral description; total parameters, active parameters and exact-model architecture remain null after original and later first-party card checks.
